name: Berlin Street Perceptions: Seven Qualities, Pairwise
description:
Method replication: participants compare pairs of Berlin street views in seven parts (order, ecology, enclosure, aesthetics, accessibility, richness, human scale), 6 pairs each, answering "Which place do you think has a higher visual …?" after a short definition of the quality. The images are not the paper's stimuli (86 Google Street View views at random points across Berlin fetched for this template, looking along the road, 2015–2025 captures).

Original study: Tian, Han, Xu, Liu, Qiu & Li (2021), "Evolution of Historical Urban Landscape with Computer Vision and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Berlin", Journal of Digital Landscape Architecture 6, 436–451. About 50 people compared random pairs from 300 Google Street View images across Berlin on eight perceived qualities in an online click-the-image survey; TrueSkill turned the choices into 0–10 scores, a model extended them to 150,000 images, and East and West Berlin districts from different periods were compared.

Differences from the original study: (1) seven of the eight qualities; "typology" (residential, office, commercial, suburban or rural) is a category rather than a more-or-less quality and is left out; (2) definitions are paraphrased from the paper's text; (3) 6 pairs per quality from 86 images.
author: Tian, Han, Xu, Liu, Qiu & Li

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: order
elements.title: Part 1 – Order: Which place do you think has a higher visual order? (Order means the geometrical sameness or repetition you can see in the place.)

elements.name: ecology
elements.title: Part 2 – Ecology: Which place do you think has a higher visual ecology? (Ecology means the presence of living things, such as plants, animals and people, and the physical environment around them.)

elements.name: enclosure
elements.title: Part 3 – Enclosure: Which place do you think has a higher visual enclosure? (Enclosure means the degree to which the street is visually defined by buildings, walls, trees and other vertical elements.)

elements.name: aesthetics
elements.title: Part 4 – Aesthetics: Which place do you think has a higher visual aesthetics? (Aesthetics means the overall visual quality of the street, being comfortable and distinct.)

elements.name: accessibility
elements.title: Part 5 – Accessibility: Which place do you think has a higher visual accessibility? (Accessibility means how easily people can reach activities, attractions and amenities from here.)

elements.name: richness
elements.title: Part 6 – Richness: Which place do you think has a higher visual richness? (Richness means the complexity of the place: the variety of buildings, landscape elements, street furniture, signs and human activity.)

elements.name: scale
elements.title: Part 7 – Human scale: Which place do you think has a higher visual human scale? (Human scale means how well the physical elements match the size and proportions of people.)
